text: The **Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes** (German Foundation for Students) is a German organization established in 1925 as a department of the Deutsche Studentenschaft. It was dissolved under National Socialism in 1934 and re-established in 1948 in Cologne. The foundation offers scholarships for undergraduate and graduate studies, as well as doctoral programs, to students who study full-time in Germany, other EU countries, or Switzerland, regardless of nationality or age. Scholarships are awarded through various nomination channels, including high schools, universities, examination boards, and national competitions, with selection based on academic excellence, initiative, and social responsibility. The scholarship includes financial support (a monthly allowance, need-based grants, and tuition support) and academic enrichment through summer schools, research groups, language courses, and mentoring. As of 2023, the foundation approved 2,179 undergraduate and graduate scholarships and 301 doctoral scholarships. Notable alumni include prominent scientists such as Manfred Eigen (Nobel Prize in Chemistry), Reinhard Genzel (Nobel Prize in Physics), and Gerd Faltings (Fields Medal), as well as leaders in business, politics, and the arts. The foundation also operates internal and open scholarship programs, including partnerships with institutions like KAUST and the Beethoven House.
